Please take notice that the Town Board of the Town of Clifton Park will conduct a public hearing on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at 7:02 PM in the Wood Memorial Meeting Room in the Town Office Building, located at One Town Hall Plaza, Town of Clifton Park, County of Saratoga, State of New York, whereas, the Town Board wishes to consider prohibiting the sale, distribution, possession for sale, and public display of Kratom and Kratom-derived products within the Town of Clifton Park. Copies of the proposed local law are posted on our website cliftonparkny.gov and is also available for review in the Town Clerk’s office during normal business hours. Caitlin Fantini, Clifton Park Town Clerk LOCAL LAW NO. of 2026 RE: A LOCAL LAW PROHIBITING THE SALE AND DISTRIBUTION OF CONCENTRATED AND SYNTHETIC 7-HYDROXYMITFRAGYNINE (7- OH) iCRATOM PRODUCTS IN THE TOWN OF CLIFTON PARK BE IT ENACTED by the Town Board-cf the Town of Clifton Park, State of New York, as follows: SECTION 1. LEGISLATIVE INFENT. Kratom, a tropical tree (Mitragyna speciosa) native to Southeast Asia, contains multiple compounds (including mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine) that act upon the same receptors in the brain as opioid drugs. These compounds produce similar effects as opioids, such as sedation, nausea, vomiting, constipation, physical dependence and-withdrawal, and respiratory depression that may lead to death. There are no drugs approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") that contain kratom, and the FDA warns that kratom is not safe for use_as a dietary supplement, citing the risk of serious adverse events suchas liver toxicity, seizures, and substance use disorder. While 7-hydroxymitragynine occurs only in trace amounts in the natural kratom leaf. concentrated _and_synthetic 7-hydroxymitragynine ("7-OH") products now sold in retail stores contain this compound at levels far exceeding those found in the plant, producing potent opioid- like effects and a heightened risk of dependence, overdose, and death. The Town Beard finds that, to protect the health and safety of Town residents, products containing elevated concentrations of 7-hydroxymitragynine should not be sold or distributed in Dutchess County. SECTION- 2. AUTHORITY, This Local Law is enacted pursuant to New York Municipal Home Rule Law § 10(1)(ii)(aj(12), as it relates to the protection, order, conduct, safety, health, and well-being of Town of Clifton Park residents. SECTION 3. DEFINITIONS. (a) "Kratom" means any part of the plant Mitragyna speciosa, whether growing or not; any compound, manufacture, salt, derivative, mixture, or preparation of such plant; all chemical compounds and alkaloids derived from such plant, including but not limited to mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine; and all synthetic and semi-synthetic derivatives of such plant, including but _not limited to MGM-15, MGM-16, and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, or any structural analogue of any such compound, derivative, mixture or alkaloid. (b) "Kxatom Product" means any product, good, article, or item containing, blended with, and/or derived from Kratom, including but_not limited to extracts, tinctures, beverages, powders, capsules: tablets, foods, gummies, vapes, and prepackaged retail items. (c) "Person" means any individual, business, company, firm, partnership, limited partnership, limited liability partnership, joint venture, corporation, not-for-profit corporation, limited liability company, estate, trust, or any other-legal entity. (d) "Prescription" means an official New York State prescription, an electronic prescription. an oral prescription, or an out-of-state prescription as those terms are used in Article 33 of the New York Public Health Law and Article 137-of the New York Education Law. (e) "Prohibited 7-OH Product" means any Kratom or Kratom- Product that contains 7- hydroxymitragynine at a level that exceeds two percent (2%) of the total alkaloids or one milligram (1 mg) per-serving. -SECTIGN 4. SALE OR DISTRIBUTION PROHIBITED. No Person may sell, offer for sale, or otherwise distribute a Prohibited 7-OH Product in the Town of Clifton Park to any other Person. This prohibition applies to any Person, including any online platform, wherever located, and a sale, offer for sale, or distribution shall be deemed to occur in the Town of Clifton Park whenever a Prohibited 7-OH Product is delivered or shipped to an address within the Town. This prohibition does not apply to the sale or distribution of a Prohibited 7-OH Product pursuant to a Prescription issued by a Person licensed, authorized, or otherwise permitted in New York State to issue a Prescription. This prohibition will not apply to the sale or distribution of a Prohibited 7-OH Product if that product is approved by the FDA. Liability under this section is strict: it shall-not be a defense to a violation that the Person did not know, or had no reason to know, that a product constituted a Prohibited 7-OH Product. SECTION 5. ENFORCEMENT AND PENALTIES, This Local Law shall be enforced by the Town Code Officers. The Safety and Security Director working with the Town Attomey are authorized to.take any and all other actions reasonable and necessary to enforce this law in accordance with the authority enumerated in the Town of Clifton Park Code including, but not limited to, conducting inspections; investigating all claims and violations: issuing all notices and orders; and any other processes that may be necessary in the enforcement of this law. Any Person that sells, offers for sale, or distributes a Prohibited 7-OH Product to another Person shall be subject to a civil penalty of not more than one thousand five hundred dollars ( $1,500) for a first violation, and not more than three thousand: dollars ($3,000) for each subsequent violation. For purposes of this section, a violation shall be considered a subsequent violation if it occurs within thirty-six (36) months of a prior violation by the same Person. Where any such sale, offer for sale, or distribution is made to a person under twenty-one (21) years of age, the maximum civil penalty for that violation shall be increased by five hundred dollars ($500). Each sale, offer for sale, or distribution ef a Prohibited 7-OH Product shall constitute a separate violation. These penalties do not apply in those-circumstances in which the sale or distribution of a Prohibited 7-OH Product is not prohibited by-this Local Law. SECTION 6. SEVERABILITY. Haw clause, sentence, paragraph, subdivision, section or part of this law of the application thereof to any person, individual, corporation, firm partnership, entity, or circumstance shall be adjudged by any court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unconstitutional, such order or judgment shall not affect, impair, or invalidate the remainder thereof, but shall be confined in its operation to the clause, sentence, paragraph, subdivision, section or part of this law, or in its application to the person, individual corporation, firm. partnership, entity, or circumstance directly involved in the controversy in which such order or judgement shall be rendered. SECTION 7. REVERSE PREEMPTION This article shall be null and void on the day that statewide legislation goes into effect incorporating either the same or substantially similar provisions as are contained in this local law or in the event that a pertinent New York State or United States of America administrative agency issues and promulgates regulations preempting such action by the Town of Clifton Park. SECTION 8. SEORA DETERMINATION. It is hereby determined, pursuant to the provisions of the New York State Environmental Quality Review Act, ECL § 8-0101, ef seq., and its implementing regulations, 6 NYCRR Part 617, that the adoption of this Local Law is a "Type II" Action within the meaning of 6 NYCRR 8§ 617.5(c)(26) and (33), and, accordingly, is of a class of actions which do not have a significant impact on the environment and no further review is required. SECTION 9, E1414ECTIVE DATE. This local law shall take effect immediately upon filing in the Office of the Secretary of State. SHORT-TERM RENTAL A short-term rental unit means an entire dwelling unit, or a room, group of rooms, other living or sleeping space, or any other space within a dwelling, made available for rentby guests for less than thirty (30) consecutive days, where the unit is offered for tourist or transient use by the short-term-rental host of the residential unit, and where such unit is located. §73-3.1 SHORT-TERM RENTALS Short-term rentals shall be subject to the following requirements: A. A short-term rental may only be operated pursuant to a permit issued by the Town of Clifton Park Department of Building and Development. B. Any permit issued for a short-term rental shall only be valid for five (5) years from the date of issuance of the permit and may be renewable on an annual basis. Any property or parcel for which an owner seeks a permit shall be subject to- an inspection by the Town of Clifton Park Department of Building and Development. Inspections shall be required on an annual basis. Such inspections shall include, but not be limited to, a fire inspection, an electrical inspection, and a septic system inspection if the property is served by private septic system. A certificate of inspection from a licensed engineer will be accepted in lieu of an inspection. Property owners may not advertise a short-term rental by placing a sign or other posting on the premises subject to the permit. The definition of Family as set forth in &208-7 of the Clifton Park Town Code shall apply to limit the occupancy of short-term rentals. Fees for-permits shall be $200 for a five (5) year period. Penalties: Any person convicted of the offense of a failure to comply with a notice of violation of the provisions of this chapter shall be subject to a fine of not less than $500, nor more than $1,000; for conviction ofa second offense, both of which were committed within a period of five years, subject to a fine of not less than $1,500" nor more than $2,500; and, upon conviction for a third or subsequent offense, all of which were committed within a period of five years, subject to a fine of not less than $5,000, nor more than $10,000. Each week or part thereof that a violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense, and the violation shall be deemed to have commenced on the earlier of the date of, or the date contained in, the notice of violation. I IP [= [O [= §73-3.2 REGISTRY [Any property in the Town of Clifton Park that is established as a "short term rental unit" at the-time of adoption of this local law, shall be exempt from the prohibitions and requirements established by this local law and shall be "grandfathered as an allowed use, further] That the owners of the-said short term unit shall submit written proof of operation and use of such short term- rental unit to the Town Clerk of the Town of Clifton Park, establishing the use of their property as a short term rental unit, with proof to consist of rental contracts, receipts or some other written proof establishing the use of the property for this stated purpose. The Town Clerk shall maintain a registry of such properties, and dates of submittal of such proof, in the Town Clerk's office, with copies to be forwarded to the Department of Building and Development, which shall. maintain a companion registry. A short-term rental may only be operated pursuant to a permit issued by the Town of Clifton Park Department of Building and Development. B. Any permit issued for a short-term rental shall only be valid for five (5) years from the date of issuance of the permit and may be renewable on an annual basis. C. Any property or parcel for which an owner seeks a permit shall be subject to- an inspection by the Town of Clifton Park Department of Building and Development. Inspections shall be required on an annual basis. Such inspections shall include, but not be limited to, a fire inspection, an electrical inspection, and a septic system inspection if the property is served by private septic system. A certificate of inspection from a licensed engineer will be accepted in lieu of an inspection. Property owners may not advertise a short-term rental by placing a sign or other posting on the premises subject to the permit. The definition of Family as set forth in &208-7 of the Clifton Park Town Code shall apply_to limit the occupancy of short-term rentals. Fees for-permits shall be $200 for a five (5) year period. Penalties: Any person convicted of the offense of a failure to comply with a notice of violation of the provisions of this chapter shall be subject to a fine of not less than $500, nor more than $1,000; for conviction ofa second offense, both of which were committed within a period of five years, subject to a fine of not less than $1,500" nor more than $2,500; and, upon conviction for a third or subsequent offense, all of which were committed within a period of five years, subject to a fine of not less than $5,000, nor more than $10,000. Each week or part thereof that a violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense, and the violation shall be deemed to have commenced on the earlier of the date of, or the date contained in, the notice of violation. text: J. The Town of East Greenbush 225 Columbia Turnpike, Rensselaer, New York 12144 TOWN BOARD AGENDA October 1, 2026 Call to Order Pledge of Allegiance Town Board Meeting: 5:00 PM Members of Town Board Present Absent Supervisor J. Conway Councilor H. Kennedy Councilor R. Matters Councilor J. McHugh Councilor L. Koenig Communications/Announcements/Reports Open Public Privilege: NOTE – Each speaker may choose to state name and address prior to addressing the Board and shall be granted the floor for up to five minutes. The Board thanks everyone in attendance for their understanding and their desire to actively participate in the decision-making process. All speakers must conduct themselves in a civil manner. Personal attacks will not be tolerated. Copies of the 2027 Tentative Budget Distributed to Town Board Members Resolutions and Proposals by Town Board Members: 199-2026 A Resolution Authorizing Sam Greco Construction Inc. to Perform Office Renovations to the Town Hall for Office Relocation Purposes WHEREAS, in an effort to streamline Town Hall operations and efficiency between departments, it has been decided that the Building Department office and Planning Department office will be consolidated and relocated into the office that currently operates as the Assessor’s Office; and WHEREAS, in order to minimize the impact and disruption to daily operations the renovation and relocation are scheduled over the long weekend of October 9th – October 12th, commonly known as Columbus Day Weekend or Indigenous People’s Day, a three-day 1 weekend, with the proviso that Town Hall is closed to the public on October 9, 2026 for a Staff Development day offsite; and WHEREAS, with the relocation and renovation of Town Hall, the Assessor’s Office will be relocated into the current Planning Department office and the Purchasing office will be relocated to the current Building Department office; and WHEREAS, Sam Greco Construction Inc., the Town’s current General Contractor, will perform the necessary renovations to make this relocation successful, including but not limited to the following: • removal of the wall in the Planning Department to expand for additional storage of file cabinets; • the removal of the wood partition between the front and back of the Planning Department; • repair the walls and carpet from the removal of those sections along with removal of cabinets adding a sink counter top in the current assessor’s office; and WHEREAS, Sam Greco construction Inc. will perform the scope of work for the amount of $15,950.00; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that this resolution will have a material impact on the Town’s finances; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board does hereby authorize Sam Greco Construction Inc. to perform the necessary improvements for the relocation of offices at Town Hall in the amount of $15,950.00. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Supervisor Conway and seconded by Councilor Kennedy and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: 200-2026 A Resolution to Appoint Dylan McLeod to the Position of Network Technician WHEREAS, the Town of East Greenbush has most recently employed Complete Network as its Information Technology (IT) provider and the contract with them expires at the end of February, 2027; and WHEREAS, Complete Network had limited experience with municipalities and no experience with police departments thus limiting their effectiveness and the Town has decided to change vendors to provide quicker and more effective responses to IT issues; and WHEREAS, the decision was made that we need an in-house full-time Town employee on site to best serve our IT needs; and WHEREAS, Dylan McLeod has been our IT provider in the past and currently fills in for Complete Network on police department issues, and has proven himself to be an experienced, extremely capable individual who knows and understands the work we do and who is very wellliked by Town staff across all departments; and 2 WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that this resolution will have a material impact for the rest of 2026 but has been budgeted for in the 2027 Tentative Budget; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board hereby appoints Dylan McLeod to the position of Network Technician for an annual salary of $90,000.00 plus $100.00 for each call-out after 6:00 p.m. on weekdays and any call-out on Saturday, Sunday or official Town holidays. and be it further RESOLVED, that this resolution will be effective as of October 15, 2026. text: TOWN OF EAST GREENBUSH ZONING BOARD OF APPEALS TOWN HALL, 225 COLUMBIA TURNPIKE, RENSSELAER, NY 12144 (518) 694-4011 FAX (518) 477-2386 MEETING AGENDA TUESDAY, OCTOBER 13, 2026 7:30PM *Meeting to be held in the Town Hall Community Room* 7:30 PM CALL TO ORDER PUBLIC HEARINGS: (ZBA# 2026-04) Patroon Place – 550 Third Ave. Ext. – Area Variance – Maximum Lot Coverage SEQR DETERMINATION & RECOMMENDATION: (ZBA# 2026-04) Patroon Place – 550 Third Ave. Ext. – Area Variance – Maximum Lot Coverage WORKSHOP/DELIBERATION: (ZBA# 2026-04) Patroon Place – 550 Third Ave. Ext. – Area Variance – Maximum Lot Coverage NEXT MEETING: October 27, 2026 APPROVAL OF MINUTES: September 22, 2026 The Town of East Greenbush PLANNING AND ZONING DEPARTMENT 225 Columbia Turnpike, Rensselaer, New York 12144 Phone: 518.694.4011 Fax: 518.477.2386 To: Jeff Pangburn, ZBA Chair From: Vincent Meade on behalf of Planning Board Chairman Mastin Re: Planning Board Recommendation Comments: The following recommendation is from the July 22, 2026 Planning Board Minutes. ZBA# 2026-04 – Patroon Place – 550 Third Avenue Extension – Area Variance Lot Coverage for Building- Report by Mike Tierney MOTION: A motion was made by Chairman Mastin as follows: Per Mr. Tierney's Report, the Planning Board makes a positive recommendation on the area variance at 550 Third Avenue Extension, strictly from a Planning perspective. * See attached report for further details. Seconded by Tierney and roll called as follows: M. MASTIN – YES; R. VIOLA – YES; C. HORNE – ABSENT; R. JUCHA – YES; M. TIERNEY – YES; J. CONWAY – YES; M. SHANLEY – YES MOTION CARRIED BY A 6-0 VOTE July 20,2026 East Greenbush Planning Board 225 Columbia Turnpike East Greenbush, NY 12061 Attn: Chairman Matt Mastin RE: Area Variance Review 2026-04 Applicant: Michael Moscatiello Patroon Place Address: 550 Third Avenue Extension Tax Map #: 144-4-49 Dear Chairman Mastin and Members of the Planning Board, Michael Moscatiello is proposing a new 10,500 sf single story storage building at the rear of this parcel. The proposed structure would be 150’ x 70’ with six storage bays. Each bay would have a 12’ x 12’ garage door. There is an existing single story retail building at the front of the parcel. The Comprehensive Zoning Law requires this project to have an Area Variance for the maximum lot coverage. Considerations in Support of the Variance Request: • Neighborhood Character: Granting the variance will not produce an undesirable change to the character of the district or be detrimental to nearby properties. There are several warehouse/ commercial businesses located near the parcel (National Grid sub station, Yankee Trails, NYISO and Garelick Farms). The proposed storage building will be located at the rear of the parcel, where the ﬁnished grade is signiﬁcantly lower than the grade along Third Ave Extension. The visual impact will be minimal from Third Ave Extension. • Alternative Methods: The applicant has demonstrated there is no feasible alternative to achieve the intended improvements without the variance. There is no other location for the proposed storage building on this parcel • Substantial Nature of the Variance: The proposed variance is not substantial or uncharacteristic for this district. The dimensions of the proposed storage building are appropriate for the parcel. • Impact on Environment and District: The proposed variance will not have an adverse effect on the physical or environmental conditions of the district as the proposed structure would be located in the rear of the parcel. • Self-Created Hardship: The hardship is not considered to be self-created. In my opinion the Area Variance is justiﬁed with the proposed 150’ x 70’ footprint. I offer a positive recommendation to grant an Area Variance for this project. Sincerely, Mike Tierney East Greenbush Planning Board 550 Third Ave Extension 550 Third Ave Extension – rear NOTICE PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that the Zoning Board of Appeals of the Town of East Greenbush will hold a public hearing on August 11, 2026 at the Town Hall 225 Columbia Turnpike Rensselaer NY beginning at 7:30 P.M. to consider the following application: Appeal number # 2026-04: The appeal of Patroon Place LLC of 99 N Greenbush Road Troy, NY 12180. The applicant proposes to construct a 11,200 sq ft warehouse on a 1.57-acre +/- lot with an existing development on site. After construction, the development would consist of 40.3% of paved area and 21.5% of building area on the lot. This will result in a combined area of 61.8% of total lot coverage. The proposal does not comply with the following provisions of the Town’s Comprehensive Zoning Law: Section 2.7.4 – Regional Commercial (RC); specifically, Subsection B, which states that the maximum lot coverage is 35%. Therefore, the proposed action requires one area variance for the property located at 550 3rd Avenue Extension, Rensselaer, NY 12144, Tax Map # 144-4-49. Any interested parties may comment in person at the hearing. Written comments may also be submitted to the Zoning Board of Appeals, Town of East Greenbush, 225 Columbia Turnpike, Rensselaer, NY 12144, at any time prior to the hearing. and WHEREAS, the Project proposes construction of an approximately 160’ x 70’, 11,200sf detached storage building containing eight (8) individually leased garage-bay storage units at the rear of the existing site, together with associated modifications to parking and internal circulation and related lighting, landscaping, screening, grading, stormwater management, and other site improvements; and WHEREAS, the existing approximately 4,372-sf commercial building located along Third Avenue Extension will remain, and no physical or operational changes to the existing building or to the existing site entrances and exits are proposed as part of the Project; and WHEREAS, the applicant has represented that the proposed garage-bay units are intended for storage rental use, with electrical service only, and that no heating, air conditioning, public water, sanitary sewer, active contractor-shop operations, manufacturing, vehicle repair, or outdoor storage is proposed as part of the Project; and WHEREAS, on July 15, 2026, the Town Board adopted Resolution 147-2026, which preliminarily classified the Project as an Unlisted Action under the State Environmental Quality Review Act (“SEQRA”), declared the Town Board’s intent to serve as Lead Agency, and initiated coordinated review pursuant to Article 8 of the Environmental Conservation Law and 6 NYCRR Part 617 based upon the Project scope and application materials then before the Town; and WHEREAS, subsequent to the initiation of coordinated review, the applicant revised the Project from six (6) proposed garage-bay units to eight (8) proposed garage-bay units and submitted updated application materials reflecting the revised scope; and WHEREAS, by Resolution 174-2026, the Town Board determined to re-initiate coordinated review of the Project in order to ensure that the Town Board and all involved and interested agencies conducted their SEQRA review based upon the same current and complete description of the proposed action; and WHEREAS, pursuant to said resolution, the revised Short Environmental Assessment Form (“SEAF”) Part 1 and relevant updated Project materials were circulated to all identified involved and interested agencies, and the applicable coordinated-review period expired without objection from any involved agency to the Town Board serving as Lead Agency; and WHEREAS, following completion of the coordinated review process, the Town Board is established as Lead Agency for the Project and has reviewed the Project as a whole, including the application materials, current site plan, SEAF Parts 1, 2 and 3, comments received from involved and interested agencies, and other materials contained within the Project record; and WHEREAS, the Town Board has compared the proposed action against the criteria set forth in 6 NYCRR §617.7(c) and has considered the potential long-term, short-term, direct, indirect, cumulative, and other reasonably related environmental impacts of the Project; and WHEREAS, the Town Board recognizes that certain technical and land use matters, including final stormwater design, parking and internal circulation, emergency access, landscaping and screening, lighting, grading, architectural treatment, and other detailed site design matters will continue to be evaluated and resolved through the Major Site Plan, Special Use Permit, area variance, and technical review processes; and WHEREAS, based upon the environmental assessment and review of the record as a whole, the Town Board finds that the Project will not result in any significant adverse environmental impacts and that preparation of an Environmental Impact Statement is not required; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that this resolution will not have a material impact on the Town’s finances; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board hereby adopts the SEAF Parts 2 and 3, as presented to the Town Board, as the supporting environmental analysis and rationale for its determination of significance; and be it further RESOLVED, that based upon its review of the entire action and the environmental record described herein, the Town Board hereby determines that the Patroon Place Project (PZD No. 26-14) will not result in any significant adverse environmental impacts, that preparation of an Environmental Impact Statement is not required, and that a Negative Declaration is hereby adopted pursuant to Article 8 of the Environmental Conservation Law and 6 NYCRR Part 617; and be it further RESOLVED, that the Town Supervisor is authorized to execute the SEAF Part 3 and any other documentation necessary to effectuate the Town Board’s determination under SEQRA; and be it further RESOLVED, that the Town Clerk and Planning and Zoning Department are hereby directed to file and maintain the Negative Declaration and related SEQRA documentation in accordance with the applicable requirements of 6 NYCRR Part 617; and be it further RESOLVED, that this resolution constitutes a determination of environmental significance under SEQRA only and does not constitute approval of the Major Site Plan, Special Use Permit, any required area variance, Building Permit, or any final site design or infrastructure plan, all of which remain subject to further review and separate action by the Town Board, Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, and other applicable agencies. Local Law Filing Pursuant to Municipal Home Rule Law §27 Local Law Number ascribed by the legislative body of the local government listed below: _ 5 __ ofthe year 2026 Local Law Title: A Local Law Amending the Code of the Town of Geneva to Adopt a New Battery Energy Storage System Law and to Amend Provisions of Chapter 165 (Zoning) Dealing with Battery Energy Storage Systems Be it enacted by the __ Town Board __ of the (Name of Legislative Body) ___ County ___City X Town ___ Village of Geneva as follows on the attached pages: For Office Use Only Department of State Local Law Index Number: ___ ofthe year20_— (The local law number assigned by the Department of State for Indexing purposes may be different from the local law number ascribed by the legislative body of the local government.) DOS-0239-a-f (Rev. 02-25) Section 1: The Code of the Town of Geneva is hereby amended with the adoption of a new Chapter 58 to read as follows: Chapter 58 Battery Energy Storage System Law 1. Authority This Battery Energy Storage System Law is adopted pursuant to Article IX of the New York State Constitution, §2(c)(6) and (10), New York Statute of Local Governments, § 10 (1) and (7); sections 261-263 of the Town Law and section 10 of the Municipal Home Rule Law of the State of New York, which authorize the Town of Geneva to adopt zoning provisions that advance and protect the health, safety and welfare of the community. 2. Statement of Purpose This Battery Energy Storage System Law is adopted to advance and protect the public health, safety, welfare, and quality of life by creating regulations for the installation and use of battery energy storage systems, with the following objectives: A. To provide a regulatory scheme for the designation of properties suitable for the location, construction and operation of battery energy storage systems; | B. To ensure compatible land uses in the vicinity of the areas affected by battery energy storage systems; C. To mitigate the impacts of battery energy storage systems on environmental resources such as important agricultural lands, forests, wildlife and other protected resources; and D. To create synergy between battery energy storage system development and the power needs of businesses and organizations that could locate in the Town with the proper infrastructure in place. 3. Definitions As used in this Chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated: ANSI: American National Standards Institute BATTERY(IES): A single cell or a group of cells connected together electrically in series, in parallel, or a combination of both, which can charge, discharge, and store energy electrochemically. For the purposes of this law, batteries utilized in consumer products are excluded from these requirements. BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM: An electronic system that protects energy storage systems from operating outside their safe operating parameters and disconnects electrical power to the energy storage system or places it ina safe condition if potentially hazardous temperatures or other conditions are detected. BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM: One or more devices, assembled together, capable of storing energy in order to supply electrical energy at a future time, not to include a stand-alone 12-volt car battery or an electric motor vehicle. A battery energy storage system is classified as a Tier 1 or Tier 2 Battery Energy Storage System as follows: A. Tier 1 Battery Energy Storage Systems have an aggregate energy capacity less than or equal to 600kWh and, if in a room or enclosed area, consist of only a single energy storage system technology. B. Tier 2 Battery Energy Storage Systems have an aggregate energy capacity greater than 600kWh or are comprised of more than one storage battery technology in a room or enclosed area. CELL: The basic electrochemical unit, characterized by an anode and a cathode, used to receive, store, and deliver electrical energy. COMMISSIONING: A systematic process that provides documented confirmation that a battery energy storage system functions according to the intended design criteria and complies with applicable code requirements. DEDICATED-USE BUILDING: A building that is built for the primary intention of housing battery energy storage system equipment, is classified as Group F-1 occupancy as defined in the NYS Uniform Code and, as applicable, International Building Code, and complies with the following: A. The building’s only use is battery energy storage, energy generation, and other electrical grid- related operations. B. No other occupancy types are permitted in the building. i } i Cc. Occupants in the rooms and areas containing battery energy storage systems are limited to personnel that operate, maintain, service, test, and repair the battery energy storage system and other : energy systems. i D. Administrative and support personnel are permitted in areas within the buildings that do not contain battery energy storage system, provided the following: 1) The areas do not occupy more than 10 percent of the building area of the story in which they are located. 2) A means of egress is provided from the administrative and support use areas to the public way that does not require occupants to traverse through areas containing battery energy storage systems or other energy system equipment. ENERGY CODE: The New York State Energy Conservation Construction Code adopted pursuant to Article 11 of the Energy Law, as currently in effect and as hereafter amended from time to time. FIRE CODE: The fire code section of the New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code adopted pursuant to Article 18 of the Executive Law, as currently in effect and as hereafter amended from time to time. B OF 2026 A LOCAL LAW TO AMEND THE TOWN OF MARCELLUS ZONING LAW TO ADD A NEW SECTION REGARDING STEEP SLOPE PROTECTIONS BE IT ENACTED by the Town Board of the Town of Marcellus as follows: SECTION 1 AUTHORITY. This local law is enacted pursuant to the New York State Constitution and New York Municipal Home Rule Law § 10. SECTION 2 AMENDMENTS TO THE TOWN OF MARCELLUS ZONING LAW TO ADD A NEW SECTION 235-26.2 (“STEEP SLOPE PROTECTIONS”). The Town of Marcellus Zoning Law is hereby amended to add Section 235-26.2 as follows: “(1) Purpose The purpose of this Steep Slope Protection Law is to conserve the sensitive environment of steep slope areas, and to regulate land use within these areas in a manner which protects the public interest by minimizing detrimental effects of land disturbance and development on steep slopes by: A. Providing for the reasonable use of steep slopes while ensuring development will not induce soil erosion, unreasonably alter the natural topography of the area, require excessive grading, increase slope instability, increase stormwater runoff, contaminate surface waters, or create onsite sewage treatment problems. B. Guarding against property damage and personal injury. Cc. Minimizing the potential for erosion, slope failure, stream siltation, increased stormwater runoff, flooding, contamination of surface waters; and protecting the water quality of Nine Mile Creek, Otisco Lake, and other downstream bodies of water. D. Conserving existing steep slope woodlands for air and water quality benefits and the preservation of wildlife habitats. (2) Definitions. CLEARING: Removing or causing to be removed the vegetation growing in the soil which protects and stabilizes the soil. Such removing or causing to be removed shall include any intentional or negligent act to (1) cut down, (2) remove all or a substantial part of, or (3) damage a tree or other vegetation which will cause the tree or other vegetation to decline and/or die. Such acts shall include but not be limited to damage inflicted upon the root system of the vegetation by the application of toxic substances, by the operation of equipment and vehicles, by storage of materials, or by the damage of natural grade due to unapproved excavation or filling, or damage caused by the unapproved alteration of natural physical conditions. The area of land disturbance of a mature tree shall be measured as the crown of the tree. LAND DISTURBANCE: Any man-made change to the land surface that may result in soil erosion from water or wind and the movement of sediments into a Watercourse, including, but not limited to, clearing, grading, excavating, transporting, and filling of Jand, paving of existing pervious areas or otherwise creating new impervious areas. WATERCOURSE: Every spring, pond (other than artificial reservoirs and filter basins), stream, creek, lake, ditch, gutter, or other channel of every kind, the waters of which will run whether continuously or occasionally. (3) Steep slope protection areas (SSPA) A. The steep slope protection areas shall include all lands having slopes 15% or greater. : B. Steep slope protection areas are further categorized as: (1) Moderately steep: 15% to less than 24.9% slope (3 to 6 in 12); (2) Very steep: 25% to less than 49.9% slope (6 to 10 in 12); and (3) Extremely steep: 50% or greater slope (> 10 in 12). Cc. The Town of Marcellus Steep Slopes map created, and as may later be amended, by the Syracuse - Onondaga County Planning Agency, the current version of which is attached hereto and incorporated herein as Exhibit “A”, shall be accepted as preliminary evidence of slope. Other scientific or reliable evidence may also be accepted as evidence of steep slope in the sole discretion of the Planning Board. D. The regulations applicable to Steep Slope Protection Areas shall be in addition to and take precedence over the zoning regulations otherwise applicable in each zoning district. (4) A. B. C. D. 6) A. Activities within a steep slope protection area requiring site plan review The following activities require site plan approval through the Town of Marcellus Planning Board, pursuant to Section 235-28, when located in a steep slope protection area. (1) Area Al: 1000 square feet or greater of land disturbance on a Moderately Steep Slope within 100 feet horizontal distance from any watercourse, (2) Area A2: 500 square feet or greater of land disturbance on a Very Steep or Extremely Steep Slope within 100 feet horizontal distance from any watercourse. (3) Area B: 3000 square feet or greater of land disturbance occurring on a Moderately Steep Slope beyond 100 horizontal feet from any watercourse. (4) Area C: 2000 square feet or greater of land disturbance occurring on a Very Steep or Extremely Steep Slope outside a Lake District and beyond 100 horizontal feet from any watercourse. Farming Operations, other than Timber Harvesting, existing as of the effective date of this Article are exempt from the site plan approval required for steep slope protection areas. All land disturbance that occurs on the steep slope protection area portion of the parcel (1) within two years or (2) that adjoins and adds to a previous area of disturbance (such as an extension of a driveway) shall be used to calculate the total area of land disturbance. Absent approval from the Planning Board, land disturbance in a steep slope protection area that exceeds the square foot limitations set forth above is prohibited. General regulations Any development proposed in a steep slope protection area shall be designed to work with the natural elements of the site, locating the proposed improvements in such a manner as to minimize land disturbance, cut and fill operations, tree removal, and alterations to natural drainage. The applicant must provide the Town Planning Board with documentation that the improvements were designed to fit the existing natural elements of the site, rather than making the site fit the development goals of the landowner as part of the site plan review process. In any project with cut and fill operations, the applicant shall prove to the Planning Board that there was no other alternative to cut and fill to develop the site and that cut, and fill has been minimized. All single-family residential land-disturbing activities in steep slope protection areas, including but not limited to clearing, grading, excavation, building construction, construction of driveways and roads, cutting, and filling, shall be limited to the minimum steep slope protection area necessary to accommodate the proposed use or activity, and shall in no case be greater than 10,000 square feet of steep slope protection area disturbance per parcel, plus land necessary for driveway access, on-site wastewater treatment system, and stormwater management facilities. Changes to the natural elevation of a steep slope development site shall be minimized. Any changes to the’ natural elevation of the site shall meet the following criteria: (1) The original, natural elevation of a steep slope protection area shall not be raised and/or lowered more than five feet on average across a contiguous area of 2,500 square feet of grading and shall not exceed 10 feet in any location in the steep slope protection area. (2) The natural elevation shall not be raised or lowered more than three feet within the required setback for structures. (3) The finished slope of all cuts or fills for any site work in areas where only vegetation is proposed to prevent erosion shail not exceed a slope of one vertical to two horizontal (50% grade or 26.5° of angle) without a retaining wall, stacked rock rip rap, or other similar structural stabilization. Any new or existing retaining wall higher than three feet above finished elevation incorporated into the proposed project design requires the evaluation of a New York licensed professional engineer, landscape architect, or architect as to its structural integrity and written direction and certification as to its use. If a permanent driveway cannot be legally built to serve the residence or other improvement, no temporary construction road/driveway may be permitted in steep slope protection areas, ; Disturbed land areas in steep slope protection areas that are not worked for seven consecutive days or more shall not be left bare or exposed. Approved temporary or permanent seeding along with protective straw mulch and/or erosion control blankets must cover these disturbed areas. All seeding, straw mulching and erosion control blankets shall meet the installation methods and quantities as stated in the New York State Standards and Specifications for Erosion and Sediment Control. Trees with a diameter of six inches or greater measured at four feet above the uphill grade (“mature trees”), when located in Areas Al and A2 on a steep slope, generally shall not be removed unless they are deemed unhealthy or a safety hazard 4 (6) by a certified arborist or equivalent. Enhancing lake views can be done through a combination of canopy reduction and selective thinning without substantial tree removal. Tree removal may be allowed in the gully zone for the purposes of traversing a gully via a bridge or culvert structure to access another portion of the property. When removal of trees exceeds the square foot land disturbance limitations set forth in section 4, the Planning Board shall consider the impact on the environment. The Planning Board may approve modifications to these standards in this law if the applicant can prove that such modifications would result in less total land disturbance and/or less change to the natural grade than would compliance with these standards and that such modifications meet the intent of this chapter to the greatest extent possible. Burden of proof The applicant shall in all cases have the burden of proof of demonstrating that the proposed activity is fully consistent with the standards for approval set forth in this law. (7) A. Steep slope protection area review process Steep slope protection area application: The steep slope protection area review process will follow the Town of Marcellus Site Plan Regulations, in addition to the following criteria: (1) The preliminary site plan and final site plan shall include the following: a. Documentation that the improvements were designed to comply with this law and have been designed to fit the existing natural elements of the site instead of altering the site to fit the development goals. b. Contours of existing and proposed conditions at vertical intervals of no more than two feet. c. Temporary roads, driveways, parking areas and pathways, including the widths and slopes of these features. d. Location of all mature trees within the proposed project limits that are located in a steep slope protection area and which, if any, of these trees will be cut as part of this project. e. An overlay of each steep slope category as defined in this local law for existing site conditions.

Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean ___ Getz ___ Lang ___ Teglash ___ 300 EMPLOYMENT MATTERS 301 Oath of Office Requirement - Each Public Officer as defined in the Public Officers Law must take the Oath of Office in accordance with Town Law Section 25 and Public Officers Law Section 10, which must be administered prior to commencing the duties of the office. text: Fair Housing – It’s Your Right! Fair housing refers to free and equal access to residential housing – i.e., housing choice. The federal Fair Housing Act makes it illegal to discriminate on the basis of a person’s race, familial status (presence of children under age 18), color, national origin, religion, disability (physical or mental), or sex. The New York State Human Rights Law protects all of the same characteristics as the federal Fair Housing Act but also makes it illegal to discriminate based on creed, age, sexual orientation, marital status, or military status. Orange County complies with the federal Fair Housing Act and the New York State Human Rights Law. The County is committed to promoting fair housing choice for all people. Fair Housing FAQ What kind of housing is covered by the Fair Housing Act? Most housing is covered by the Fair Housing Act. In some circumstances, the Act exempts owner-occupied buildings with no more than four units, single family housing sold or rented without the use of a broker, and housing operated private clubs that limit occupancy to members. In New York State, fair housing laws cover most housing, with three main exceptions: One- or two-family owner-occupied buildings; Room rentals in housing for individuals of the same sex; and Room rentals in owner-occupied housing. Illegal Actions Fair housing laws apply to the sale or rental of housing and also to mortgage lending. They cover some very specific actions. Some typical examples include Refusing to rent, sell, finance, insure, or negotiate for housing; Making housing unavailable; Setting different terms or conditions, or providing unequal services; Printing or circulating a discriminatory advertisement; Refusing to make or provide information for a loan, or imposing different terms or conditions for a loan; or Harassing, threatening, intimidating, or coercing anyone, including sexual harassment. Those with Disabilities Are Protected Under the fair housing laws, a landlord may not: Refuse to make reasonable modifications to a dwelling or common use area to accommodate a person’s disability; or Refuse to make reasonable accommodations in policies or services if necessary for the disabled person to use the housing. In addition, any multi-family housing built after 1991 must comply with accessibility requirements to ensure that public and common use areas and units are accessible for people with disabilities. Fair Housing Links Laws New York Human Rights Law: https://dhr.ny.gov/law Federal Fair Housing Act Link: https://www.justice.gov/crt/fair-housing-act-2 Who can I contact if I believe I’ve been discriminated against? Complaints related to discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or familial status may also be filed directly with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). What information do I need to provide to file a fair housing complaint? If you suspect that you have been discriminated against with regard to housing, file a complaint as soon as possible because there are time limits on when a complaint can be filed with HUD after an alleged violation. Try to include the following information, if possible, when filing a complaint: ▪ The name and address; ▪ The name and address of the person(s) or Company the complaint is against; ▪ The address or other identifying information of the housing or program the complaint is being filed against; ▪ A brief description of what happened that caused you to file the complaint; and ▪ The date(s) of the alleged discrimination. How can I file a fair housing complaint? Fair housing complaints can be filed with HUD by telephone, online, email and by mail. Phone 1-800-669-9777 (1-800-927-9275 for TTY users only) Online English: https://portalapps.hud.gov/FHEO903/Form903/Form903Start.action Spanish: https://portalapps.hud.gov/AdaptivePages/HUD_Spanish/Espanol/complaint/complaintdetails.htm Other languages: https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/complaint_filing_languages_othe r_english If you have questions or believe you have been a victim of housing discrimination, you may also contact the Civil Rights Bureau of the New York State Attorney General's Office at 212-416-8250 or civil.rights@ag.ny.gov. Repairing the Damage If discrimination has taken place, the laws direct that steps may be taken to remedy the situation. This can include requiring changes in policies and practices; Making the housing or loan available; Assessing money damages and/or attorney fees; or Imposing civil fines and penalties.

text: TOWN OF WILTON 22 Traver Road, Wilton, New York 12831 Code and Zoning Revision Committee LOCAL LAW NO. __ OF 2026 A LOCAL LAW ADDING CHAPTER 41 TO THE CODE OF THE TOWN OF WILTON, ENTITLED "AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE READER SYSTEMS" Be it enacted by the Town Board of the Town of Wilton as follows: Section 1. Chapter 41 added. Chapter 41 of the Code of the Town of Wilton is hereby added to read as follows: CHAPTER 41 AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE READER SYSTEMS § 41-1. Findings; purpose; statutory authority. A. The Town Board finds that automated license plate reader systems systematically collect information concerning the location and movement of motor vehicles, including vehicles whose owners or occupants are not suspected of criminal or unlawful activity. B. The Town Board further finds that the aggregation, retention, analysis and sharing of such information can create detailed records concerning the movements and associations of residents and visitors and can expose such information to misuse, unauthorized access, data breaches or disclosure to third parties. C. The Town Board finds that the widespread deployment of automated license plate reader systems presents risks to individual privacy, freedom of movement, freedom of association, data security and public confidence in government. D. The purpose of this Chapter is therefore to prohibit systematic automated license plate recognition and vehicle-location surveillance within the Town while preserving the lawful use of ordinary security cameras and narrowly tailored access-control systems that do not create or contribute to databases tracking vehicles traveling through the community. E. This Chapter is intended to regulate a category of technology and conduct and shall apply without regard to the manufacturer, vendor, owner or operator of the technology. F. This Chapter is adopted pursuant to § 10 of the Municipal Home Rule Law and §§ 130 and 135 of the Town Law. § 41-2. Definitions. For purposes of this Chapter: AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE READER SYSTEM or ALPR SYSTEM Any system, device, camera, software, computer algorithm or combination thereof that automatically photographs, scans, identifies, recognizes, converts, records or analyzes a motor vehicle license plate or other vehicle-identifying characteristic into computer-readable data and associates such information with a date, time or location for the purpose of creating, maintaining, contributing to or querying a searchable record or database. The term includes fixed, mobile, portable and vehicle-mounted systems and systems capable of identifying vehicles by license plate number, make, model, color or other distinguishing characteristics. CAPTURED PLATE DATA Any license plate number, vehicle image, date, time, location, direction of travel, vehicle characteristic or other information captured by, derived from or inferred through an ALPR system. FIXED OR PERMANENTLY INSTALLED Affixed to or mounted upon a pole, building, structure, trailer, ground mount or other stationary support, and operated from a stationary position, whether or not the support is itself capable of being relocated. PERSON Includes an individual, corporation, limited-liability company, partnership, limited partnership, business trust, estate, trust, association, or any other legal or commercial entity of any kind or description. SECURED AREA An area that is not open to the general public, is enclosed or otherwise subject to defined boundaries, and may ordinarily be entered only through designated access-control points. TOWN ENTITY The Town of Wilton and every department, board, office, agency, employee, official, agent or contractor acting for or on behalf of the Town. [Drafter's note] The definition of "person" is taken verbatim from § 43-2 so that the two chapters read consistently. § 41-3. Prohibited acts. A. No person shall, within the Town of Wilton, install, deploy, operate, maintain or use an automated license plate reader system that collects, or is capable of collecting, data concerning vehicles while they are located within the Town. B. No person shall knowingly cause captured plate data to be collected in violation of this Chapter. No person who collected captured plate data in violation of this Chapter, caused its collection, or owned or operated the ALPR system through which it was collected shall retain, sell, license, exchange, transmit or disclose such data, except as required by law. C. No Town Entity shall acquire, lease, contract for, subscribe to, accept as a donation, install, operate, access, query or use an ALPR system, captured plate data, or any ALPR database, whether regional, statewide, national, commercial or privately operated; and no Town funds, property, rights-of-way, easements, poles, facilities, equipment or other Town resources shall be used to install, operate, maintain or facilitate an ALPR system. D. The prohibitions of this section apply regardless of whether the equipment is owned by the person operating it, leased from a third party, supplied without charge, or whether the resulting data are stored within or outside the Town. [Mark Question] Subsection B and § 41-5(E) restrict retention and disclosure only by the person who collected the data, caused its collection, or owned or operated the system. They do not reach a person who later receives the data without participating in its collection, such as a journalist, researcher or attorney. In Bartnicki v. Vopper, 532 U.S. 514 (2001), the Supreme Court held that the First Amendment protected disclosure of unlawfully intercepted communications on a matter of public concern by persons who did not participate in the interception. Please confirm this limitation is sufficient. § 41-4. Exclusions. The prohibitions of this Chapter shall not apply to: A. A conventional photographic or video surveillance camera that may incidentally capture an image of a license plate but does not automatically convert, identify, index or analyze license plates or vehicle characteristics into searchable computer-readable data. B. A dashboard camera, body-worn camera, doorbell camera or similar recording device, provided that no functionality that would cause the device to constitute an ALPR system under § 41-2 is enabled or used. C. A system used solely to control physical entry into or exit from a secured area that is not open to the general public, provided that: 1. the data are used only for access control or security of that secured area; 2. the data are not contributed or made accessible to a commercial, regional, statewide or national ALPR database or vehicle-location network; and 3. the data are not disclosed except with the consent of the vehicle owner or pursuant to lawful judicial process. § 41-5. Existing systems. A. Notwithstanding § 41-3(A), an ALPR system in operation within the Town on the effective date of this Chapter shall not be deemed in violation of this Chapter during the compliance periods established by this section, provided that its owner and operator comply with this section. B. Every such system shall cease collecting captured plate data no later than thirty (30) days after the effective date of this Chapter. C. No later than sixty (60) days after the effective date of this Chapter, the owner or operator of any fixed or permanently installed ALPR system shall either physically remove the equipment from the premises and certify such removal in writing to the Code Enforcement Officer, or obtain a certificate of decommissioning under Subsection D. D. The Code Enforcement Officer shall issue a certificate of decommissioning only upon written application by the owner or operator of the system and upon determining, on the basis of documentation submitted by the applicant and any inspection conducted under this subsection, that all functionality that would cause the device to constitute an ALPR system under § 41-2 has been permanently removed or disabled and that the device is not connected to any ALPR database or vehiclelocation network. The Code Enforcement Officer may require that such documentation include written confirmation from the vendor, installer or a qualified technician, and may inspect the device with the consent of the owner of the premises and the owner of the device, pursuant to a warrant or court order obtained from a court of competent jurisdiction, or as otherwise authorized by law. The certificate shall be revoked if the device is restored to operation as an ALPR system. E. The owner and operator of a system subject to this section shall not sell, transfer, upload or disclose captured plate data collected through that system within the Town, except as required by law. [Drafter's note] Because § 41-4(A) permits ordinary security cameras, this section does not require removal of hardware that can lawfully remain in service once its ALPR functionality is gone. Removal and a certificate are the only two ways to comply with Subsection C, so switching a system off or suspending its service does not satisfy it. The certificate test in Subsection D is tied to the § 41-2 definition so that a device which stops reading plates but continues to identify vehicles by appearance does not qualify. [For Mark] The certificate is deliberately not conditioned on advance consent to inspection. In Sokolov v. Village of Freeport, 52 N.Y.2d 341 (1981), the Court of Appeals held unconstitutional a permit scheme that effectively compelled consent to warrantless inspection, and a mandatory consent condition would raise the same question here. Verification therefore rests on documentation the applicant must supply, with inspection available by consent, by warrant or court order, or as otherwise authorized by law. The warrant language follows the Code’s existing usage in Chapters 43 and 69. Because the equipment owner and the owner of the premises may be different persons, Subsection D requires the consent of both for a consensual inspection. Please confirm this structure is sound. [For Mark] Note an intentional asymmetry in this section. Subsection B requires every existing ALPR system, fixed or mobile, to stop collecting within thirty days. The removal and decommissioning obligations in Subsections C and D apply only to fixed or permanently installed systems, because there is no coherent way to order the physical removal of equipment mounted on a vehicle that merely passes through the Town. A mobile operator is therefore subject to the prohibition and the penalties but not to the certificate process. Please confirm this is a defensible structure. § 41-6. Enforcement and penalties. A. This Chapter shall be enforced by the Code Enforcement Officer and all other code enforcement personnel as defined in § 43-2, and by any other officer or employee designated by the Town Board. B. Penalties. (1) Any person who violates any provision of this Chapter, or any term or condition of a certificate or order issued pursuant to this Chapter, shall be guilty of a violation punishable by a fine of not more than $1,000. (2) Any person who violates any provision of this Chapter shall also be liable to pay a civil penalty of not more than $1,000, recoverable in an action instituted in the name of the Town of Wilton. (3) Each camera or other discrete image-capture device installed, operated, maintained or used as part of an ALPR system shall constitute a separate violation. Following written notice of a violation and expiration of any applicable compliance period, each day that an unlawful ALPR system remains in operation or remains installed upon the premises shall constitute a separate violation. C. Injunctive relief. Upon authorization of the Town Board, the Town may commence an action or proceeding in a court of competent jurisdiction to compel compliance with this Chapter, restrain any violation by temporary or permanent injunction, require the removal of any ALPR system installed or operated in violation of this Chapter, or obtain any other remedy available at law or in equity. D. The owner of property upon which an ALPR system is installed and the person operating or controlling the system may each be held responsible where such person knowingly permits or continues the violation following notice thereof. E. Notwithstanding §§ 43-4(G) and 43-7(B) of this Code, no building permit, sign permit or certificate of occupancy shall be issued for premises upon which a violation of this Chapter is known to exist. This subsection applies only to the premises upon which the violation exists. F. Remedies not exclusive. The remedies and penalties provided in this section are cumulative, and each is in addition to any other remedy or penalty available under this Code or other applicable law. [For Mark] Subsection E is limited to building permits, sign permits and certificates of occupancy for the premises where the violation exists. Variances, special use permits and site plan approvals are deliberately excluded: Town Law § 267-b prescribes the criteria a Zoning Board must apply to variance applications, and § 274-a limits site plan conditions to those reasonably and directly related to the site plan. Within the Code, the subsection follows § 129-171, which already bars issuance of a building permit on property where a zoning violation is known to exist, and sign permits are already conditioned by § 129-187(A)(1) on compliance with all other laws and ordinances of the Town. Because §§ 43-4(G) and 43-7(B) direct that a building permit and a certificate of occupancy shall issue upon Uniform Code and Energy Code compliance, Subsection E expressly overrides those sections. Please confirm that approach satisfies Municipal Home Rule Law § 22, or advise whether conforming amendments to Chapter 43 should be added as a separate section of this local law. [For Mark] Subsections B, C and F follow the structure of § 43-17, which provides both a fine and a civil penalty of up to $1,000, requires Town Board authorization for injunctive actions, and makes remedies cumulative. Unlike § 43-17(C), this Chapter provides no term of imprisonment. Because each device and each day is a separate violation, daily exposure multiplies with the number of noncompliant devices at a premises. The $1,000 figure matches the highest penalty found anywhere in the Code. Because justice court civil jurisdiction is limited to $3,000, an accumulated civil penalty above that amount would be pursued in Supreme Court, most practically together with an injunctive action under Subsection C. Please confirm the $1,000 figure is within the Town’s authority under Municipal Home Rule Law § 10(4)(b) and Town Law § 135, that providing both a fine and a civil penalty for the same violation is appropriate here as it is in Chapter 43, and whether a higher amount would be permissible should the Town Board wish to adopt one. [For Mark] Appearance-ticket authority is deliberately omitted. Municipal Home Rule Law § 10(4)(a) permits a local law to authorize non-police public servants to issue appearance tickets only in enumerated subject areas, such as building, zoning and planning, and this Chapter does not clearly fall within them. Enforcement can proceed by a document filed in Town Court on the Code Enforcement Officer’s sworn allegations, or through the Sheriff. Please advise whether authority exists to add it. § 41-7. Severability. If any clause, sentence, paragraph, subsection, section or application of this Chapter is adjudged by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or preempted, such judgment shall not affect, impair or invalidate the remainder of this Chapter or its application to other persons or circumstances. § 41-8. Effective date. This local law shall take effect immediately upon filing in the office of the New York State Secretary of State in accordance with Section 27 of the Municipal Home Rule Law, subject to the compliance periods specified in § 41-5. Notes for Mark [Municipal authority] Please confirm that the Town’s police powers under Municipal Home Rule Law § 10 and Town Law § 130 authorize a townwide prohibition on the private installation and operation of automated license plate reader systems, including systems located wholly upon private commercial property and collecting data only from vehicles present on that property, and identify any preemption, State constitutional, or other limitations on that authority. Every other question in this Chapter is secondary to this one, as the whole thing is dead in the water if the Town lacks authority to reach private collection on private property, If so, the Chapter would need to be rebuilt around Town property, Town rights-of-way, and Town use, which the Town plainly can regulate. [First Amendment] Two opposing decisions frame the question, which tells me that we at least have a leg to stand on should there be a challenge. In Sorrell v. IMS Health Inc., 564 U.S. 552, the Supreme Court applied heightened scrutiny to a Vermont statute restricting the sale, disclosure and use of prescriber-identifying data, reasoning that the creation and dissemination of information is speech. In Western Watersheds Project v. Michael, 869 F.3d 1189, the Tenth Circuit relied on Sorrell to hold that the collection of data may itself constitute protected creation of speech, observing that a contrary rule would let government regulate the source of information instead of its dissemination. Neither is a Second Circuit ALPR decision and neither controls here. A prohibition on collection is not demonstrably safer than a restriction on data sharing, and this Chapter is not on settled ground either way.

text: TOWN OF WILTON, NEW YORK Chapter ___ OUTDOOR LIGHTING § ___-1. Purpose and intent. The purpose of this chapter is to establish regulations for outdoor lighting that provide appropriate illumination levels for safety and security while minimizing the adverse effects of excessive or poorly directed lighting, including light trespass, light pollution, glare, and sky glow. It is the intent of this chapter to preserve the rural and suburban character of the Town, to protect the health and welfare of its residents and natural environment, and to promote energy conservation through the reasonable regulation of outdoor lighting on all properties within the Town of Wilton. § ___-2. Applicability. A. This chapter shall apply to all outdoor lighting on all properties in all zoning districts within the Town of Wilton. B. Outdoor lighting associated with uses subject to site plan review or special use permit approval shall comply with both this chapter and any additional lighting conditions imposed by the approving board. C. This chapter shall not apply to: (1) Temporary lighting used by law enforcement, fire, or emergency services in the performance of their duties. (2) Lighting required by the Federal Aviation Administration or other federal or state agency. (3) Lighting installed by the Town of Wilton, Saratoga County, or the State of New York on public roadways or public property. (4) Outdoor lighting existing as of the effective date of this chapter, except as provided in § ___-7 of this chapter. (5) Temporary lighting associated with active construction, provided such lighting is removed upon completion of construction activity and is aimed, shielded, or otherwise mitigated to the extent practicable, consistent with applicable safety requirements, to minimize light trespass and glare onto adjacent properties and public roadways. § ___-3. Definitions. As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated: CORRELATED COLOR TEMPERATURE (CCT) A measure, in degrees Kelvin (K), of the color appearance of light emitted by a lamp or fixture. DIRECT LIGHT Light emitted by a fixture from a lamp, from a reflector, or through a refractor. FACADE LIGHTING Permanent outdoor fixtures that are specifically intended to illuminate the exterior surfaces of buildings or structures. FIXTURE A complete lighting unit, including a lamp together with the parts designed to distribute the light, to position and protect the lamp, and to connect the lamp to the power supply. FLOOD- OR SPOTLIGHT Any fixture or lamp that incorporates a reflector or a refractor to concentrate the light output into a directed beam in a particular direction. FULLY SHIELDED FIXTURE A fixture that allows no direct light from the fixture above a horizontal plane through the fixture’s lowest light-emitting part in its mounted position. GLARE Light emitted by a fixture with intensity sufficient to cause annoyance, discomfort, or reduced visibility to a person on or off the property. HEIGHT OF LUMINAIRE The vertical distance from the ground directly below the centerline of the luminaire to the lowest direct light-emitting part of the luminaire. INDIRECT LIGHT Direct light that has been reflected or scattered off of other surfaces. LAMP A light bulb or other component of a fixture that changes electricity into visible light. LIGHT POLLUTION The inappropriate or excessive use of artificial light, including sky glow, glare, light trespass, and energy waste. LIGHT TRESPASS Light from an artificial source that falls beyond the property boundary of the property on which the light source is located and onto property that it is not intended to illuminate. LUMEN A unit of measurement of the total quantity of visible light emitted by a lamp or fixture, as measured. OUTDOOR LIGHTING The nighttime illumination of an outside area or object by any artificial device located outdoors that produces light by any means. SKY GLOW A brightening of the night sky caused by artificial light directed upward or sideways, reducing one’s ability to view the night sky. § ___-4. General lighting standards. All outdoor lighting installed after the effective date of this chapter shall comply with the following standards: A. Light trespass prohibited. No outdoor light fixture or lamp shall be installed, aimed, or operated so as to cause direct light or glare to fall beyond the property boundary of the property on which the fixture is located. B. Color temperature. Outdoor lighting fixtures installed after the effective date of this chapter are recommended to have a correlated color temperature (CCT) not exceeding 3000 Kelvin. C. Timers, sensors, and dimmers. Where practicable, outdoor lighting installations are encouraged to include timers, motion sensors, and dimmers to reduce energy consumption and unnecessary illumination during overnight hours. D. Upward-directed lighting. Outdoor lighting, including floodlights and spotlights, directed upward shall be aimed at a specific building, architectural feature, landscape element, or flag and shall not be directed into open sky. Upward-directed fixtures shall not exceed 900 lumens per fixture. § ___-5. Operation as nuisance prohibited. A. No outdoor light or lights shall be installed or operated so as to constitute a nuisance. For the purposes of this chapter, a nuisance shall be characterized by any lamp or fixture that: (1) Exceeds 900 lumens and is not fully shielded or aimed so as to prevent light trespass beyond the property boundary or directly into open sky; or (2) Is directed toward or creates glare upon any public roadway so as to impair the vision of motorists; or (3) Is directed toward or illuminates the interior of any adjacent property; or (4) Consists of multiple fixtures that in combination produce light trespass, glare, or illumination of adjacent properties sufficient to constitute a nuisance under subsections (1) through (3) above. B. The investigation of a complaint under this section shall be initiated in response to a written complaint submitted to the Code Enforcement Officer. § ___-6. Additional standards for nonresidential and multifamily uses. In addition to the general standards of § ___-4, outdoor lighting for nonresidential uses, multifamily residential developments, and uses subject to site plan review or special use permit approval shall comply with the following: A. A photometric lighting plan shall be submitted as part of any site plan or special use permit application, showing the location, type, height, aiming direction, shielding, lumen output, and color temperature of all proposed outdoor fixtures. B. Parking area lighting shall utilize fully shielded fixtures with a maximum pole height of 30 feet. C. Upward-directed lighting prohibited. No outdoor lighting on nonresidential or multifamily properties shall be directed upward toward the sky, except for temporary, permitted public event lighting. Facade lighting shall be directed downward from above the surface to be illuminated and shall not spill beyond the building façade. § ___-7. Applicability to existing lighting. A. Outdoor lighting lawfully in existence as of the effective date of this chapter that does not conform to the provisions hereof shall not be required to be brought into compliance solely by reason of the adoption of this chapter. B. Replacement or substantial modification of an existing nonconforming outdoor lighting fixture shall require the replacement fixture to comply with all provisions of this chapter. C. Notwithstanding subsection A, any existing outdoor lighting that is determined by the Code Enforcement Officer to constitute a nuisance under § ___-5 shall be required to be brought into compliance with the provisions of this chapter within 30 days of written notice from the Code Enforcement Officer. § ___-8. Enforcement. A. The Code Enforcement Officer, or a duly authorized designee, shall be responsible for the enforcement of this chapter, upon written complaint. B. Whenever the Code Enforcement Officer determines that a violation of this chapter exists, the Code Enforcement Officer shall issue a written notice to the property owner or responsible person. Such notice shall: (1) Be in writing; (2) Include a description of the property sufficient for identification; (3) Include a statement of the violation and the specific provision(s) of this chapter that have been violated; (4) Set a reasonable time, not less than 30 days from the date of notice, for compliance, or such longer period as the Code Enforcement Officer determines reasonable based on the nature and scope of the required corrective action; and (5) Be served upon the property owner or occupant personally or by registered mail or certified mail. C. If, upon reinspection after the expiration of the compliance period, the violation has not been corrected, the Code Enforcement Officer is authorized to commence an enforcement action in the appropriate court. § ___-9. Penalties for offenses. A. A violation of any provision of this chapter shall, upon conviction thereof, be punishable by a fine not to exceed $350 for a first offense, $700 for a second offense within 18 months of the first offense, and $1,000 for each subsequent offense within 18 months of the first offense. B. Each day that a violation continues after the expiration of the compliance period set forth in the notice of violation shall constitute a separate offense. § ___-10. Severability. If any section, subsection, clause, phrase, or provision of this chapter, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, shall be adjudged invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, such determination shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions of this chapter. § ___-11. Effective date. This chapter shall take effect immediately upon filing with the Secretary of State.
